semantic_checks.finding: The retained family is padded outside s with the strict harmless inequality 0<1. Actual minimal-subfamily selection is reused, and a deleted-inequality witness would force 1<0 if an outside index were selected. Thus all selected indices really lie in s, the selection is injective, and the hard event is preserved exactly.

Tied duplicate normalized inequalities are not differentiated in their original nonsmooth coordinate list. Exact selection plus irredundancy excludes retaining two copies of the same supporting halfspace: their simultaneous boundary levels would contradict actual pair affine inconsistency. Each actual tangent facet is selected once. The zero selected-count case is permitted.

An affine point on the two supporting planes is fixed by the successive Gaussian sections. Together with the exact residual dot identity, this proves a true strict residual interior witness, not a generic-threshold condition or an assumed boundary identity.

The raw residual support level is proved at an actual common support point. Dividing by the actual residual normal scale gives the signed tangential support distance; no absolute value or sign reversal is introduced.

The pointwise pair Green formula begins with the genuine signed pair-section decomposition into (a^2+c^2-2) times section probability plus the residual radial trace. Exact event equality transports that trace to the selected presentation, and the proved pointwise radial identity is applied there. Original tied coordinate partials never replace the selected derivatives.

The arbitrary-presentation theorem assumes only an exact hard-event equivalence, strict interior, and deletion witnesses. The normalized identity multiplies by an arbitrary signed scalar W and keeps the exact minus boundary sign. The conversion threshold*finiteFirst=distance*boundaryMass cancels precisely the inverse residual-normal-length Jacobian.

HasStrictRidgeInterior has the ordinary two-active-original-support-planes and all-other-inequalities-strict meaning. Its equivalence with strict residual interior is proved in both directions using actual native pair levels and the pair-base dot identity. Distinct actual original facet witnesses supply a nonparallel pair before constructing the presentation.

ActualRidgeFacetPresentation contains only count/index bounds, injectivity, retained membership, exact event equivalence, strict interior, and irredundancy witnesses. It has no Green, quantitative surface estimate, common mass, incidence or spherical identity field. normals/levels/outwardConormal/signedDistance/boundaryMass are concrete derived data.

The native Green theorem is obtained by instantiating the actual-presentation analytic identity with the native orthonormal pair and the genuine angle times two-normal Gaussian density. It keeps signed distance and all selected masses; no full-family independence or threshold-generic premise is present.

For a nonactual pair, the proof derives the ordinary residual no-zero-boundary condition from actual original facet witnesses, then applies the actual fixed-threshold Gaussian nullity theorems. Both the signed and leading section terms are zero. Parallel or diagonal guards are separately handled by the actual native definitions.

A strict supporting point is constructed by interpolation between a strict interior point and an actual deleted-inequality witness. The coefficient is genuinely in (0,1), its selected level is exact, and all other selected constraints remain strict. Pullback through the actual pair base gives all original inequalities weakly, the three selected equalities, and other selected strict inequalities. Deleted original inequalities may remain active, so arbitrary nonsimple extra active facets are allowed.

The selected outward conormal is proved unit, orthogonal to both native pair normals, and positively scaled from the true residual normal. Its Gaussian section lies exactly on the selected residual supporting plane. These are concrete geometric identities rather than additional presentation fields.

On the selected conormal section, the missing selected inequality is restored using its exact support equality. P.event_iff then restores every retained original inequality, including deleted or tied ones. The original j/l inequalities are restored by the actual pair-base support equations. This gives the full original closed hard event, without an unjustified strictness replacement.

The resulting mass identity is exactly phi(alpha)*phi(beta)*boundaryMass=gaussianFrameHardMass of the full original event in the selected native triple frame. The scalar conormal density is phi(distance); the triple-frame normal density has no additional Gram denominator. The exact orthogonal section-point identity proves the integral transport, rather than matching only a covariance or a marginal mass.

All statements are at a fixed threshold under ordinary geometric hypotheses. The actual 300-node proof graph has no dependency on SurfaceFatou, ActualRidgeEstimates, the threshold-AE pair-regularity theorem or the threshold-AE native ridge Green theorem. Spatial Gaussian-null facts and ordinary analytic Gaussian differentiation are used legitimately; there is no threshold-genericity, Fatou continuation or target Green premise.
